disposition_reason: Per-sample arsenic, cadmium, mercury and lead results for eight breakfast cereal brands are shown only as bar figures (Figures 2-5); the text gives only approximate ranges and the abstract states them in µg/L of digest, so no concentration can be recorded.

study.design: retail survey of eight breakfast cereal brands
study.market: local retail outlets, United Arab Emirates
study.method: HNO3 digestion, dilution in 1% HNO3, ICP-MS (PerkinElmer DRC-e), triplicate aliquots
study.qa: calibration verified with certified aqueous standards (Fluka 70007, QC2-1, Table 1); no food CRM; RSD <5%

unresolved: Values are figure-only (Figures 2-5); not read off bars.

Text gives approximate ranges only: As 'range 100-180ppb' with sample 7 '>800ppb'; Cd 'about 10-60ppb'; Hg 'about 250-400ppb'; Pb two samples elevated, sample 7 more than five times the limit. Abstract gives As 100-900, Cd 8-50, Hg 270-370, Pb 115-30000 µg/L (digest units), which conflict with the ppb text; none recorded.
Mercury at 250-400 ppb in cereals is implausibly high for food and is not corroborated by QA on a food matrix.
Sample mass, dilution and basis not stated.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Limits quoted by authors: As 1400 ppb solid foods, Cd 100 ppb cereals, Hg 500 ppb foodstuff
